subject: Approval request: custom audit cadence & egress lock for Helios Labs
messages:
From: Marta Suarez <marta@helioslabs.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@helioslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: audit cadence & egress lock requirement (Helios Labs)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Helios is excited about the performance profile on the dedicated stacks. A couple of procurement/legal asks surfaced while we reviewed the SOW and security spreadsheet:

1) Network egress lock: we need a strictly enforced egress-control configuration (no outbound internet from the VPC except to our monitoring endpoints) and a mechanism to apply it at deployment time.
2) Audit cadence & access: because of our regulated customers we need audit access with a 5-day snapshot window available on request; ideally monthly for the first 6 months, then quarterly thereafter. Audit team would be a combination of internal Helios auditors and an approved third-party auditor.
3) Commercial concession: given the extra operational work and the restricted deployment constraints, procurement is asking for a 2% first-year credit on committed spend (applied to monthly invoices).

I've attached the security questionnaire and a SOW draft for context. Can you confirm if Redwood can: (a) lock egress at deployment and provide a configuration template, (b) accommodate the audit cadence and third-party access under a written agreement, and (c) route the ask for the commercial concession / credit to the appropriate approver?

Appreciate a quick read — procurement has a target signature by April 16.

Best,
Marta Suarez
Head of IT Security
Helios Labs

Attachments: Helios_Security_Questions_2027.xlsx, SOW-Draft-Helios-v1.docx
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Marta Suarez <marta@helioslabs.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: audit cadence & egress lock requirement (Helios Labs)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the attachments.

Quick answers up front:
- Egress lock: yes, our Private deployment supports strict egress rules enforced at the orchestration layer; we can provide a deployment manifest and a test checklist.
- Audit cadence: we can provide audit snapshots but need to align on scope (logs, runbooks, access method).
- Commercial concession: needs deal-desk / exec approval — looping in Priyom (sales) and Laura (legal) to scope the ask and escalate.

Priyom / Laura — see Marta's asks (quoted below). Procurement is asking for monthly snapshots for 6 months then quarterly, and a 2% first-year credit. Can we get an initial read from legal on the audit wording and from sales on whether the proposed credit is within our deal desk guardrails? If needed I can prepare a short exec memo.

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Marta Suarez <marta@helioslabs.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: audit cadence & egress lock requirement (Helios Labs)

Hi team — quick internal take before legal provides formal language.

Commercials: a 2% first-year credit is slightly outside standard net-new deal guardrails for Private deployments. We can consider a 1–1.5% credit if the customer commits to a 12-month reserved capacity and accepts a reasonable audit scope. I recommend we offer 1.5% conditional on 12mo commit and a shared-cost third-party audit arrangement.

Audit cadence & logistics: we can provision monthly snapshots for the first 3 months (not 6) because of operational overhead, then quarterly. For Helios's ask of a 5-day snapshot availability, propose a 10-business-day audit window with prioritized scheduling for the first quarter. That gives our Ops team predictable lead time and still meets Helios's compliance needs.

Action: can Laura confirm whether a 10-business-day window + third-party auditor with an NDA and audit proxy would be acceptable? If yes, I'll prepare the commercial memo and escalate to Markus for exec approval on the adjusted credit.

— Priyom
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: audit cadence & egress lock requirement (Helios Labs)

Hi Marta / team — thanks for the details and the attachments. I reviewed the security questionnaire and the proposed SOW language. High level legal position below.

1) Egress lock: acceptable. We will provide a deployment manifest and hardened orchestration template. We will document permitted endpoints (Helios monitoring and agreed vendor telemetry) and include a test plan.

2) Audit access & cadence: we cannot commit to unlimited snapshot retention or unrestricted live access. Proposed legal compromise:
- Audit proxy: Helios may appoint an approved third-party auditor (subject to an NDA). Redwood will provide timebound access to relevant logs and artefacts via a controlled audit proxy.
- Notice & window: 10 business days' notice minimum; Redwood will provide requested snapshots or access within that window. For the first 3 months we can prioritize scheduling and reduce the notice period where operationally feasible.
- Scope: logs, runbooks, and configuration manifests only; no direct access to production workloads or raw customer data beyond redacted logs.

3) Commercial concession: providing a first-year credit requires executive approval. If sales recommends a 1–1.5% credit tied to a 12-month reserved commitment and shared-cost audit, legal can draft the amendment.

Next steps:
- Aditya / Priyom: please confirm if Helios will accept a 1.5% credit conditional on 12mo commit and the audit proxy arrangement.
- Markus: requesting your exec approval to sign off on the 1.5% credit as an exception to standard pricing. If you prefer, I will draft a one-page memo summarizing the legal constraints and risk considerations.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
